definitions.gloss: gluten-free; (of food, ingredients, or a diet) not containing gluten, the protein found in wheat, barley, and rye
definitions.explanation: The English-derived loanword for 'gluten-free'. It is used both as a noun and as an attributive modifier, often before another noun (e.g. グルテンフリーの{食事|しょくじ} 'a gluten-free meal', グルテンフリー{食品|しょくひん} 'gluten-free foods'). It can also be used predicatively, meaning that something 'is gluten-free'. In Japan it commonly refers to specialty foods made without wheat for people with celiac disease, wheat allergies, or those choosing the diet for health or fitness reasons.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦パン→パン：00553_pan⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧グルテンフリーです。
⟦{米粉|こめこ}→米粉：13771_komeko⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{使|つか}った→使う：00473_tsukau⟧グルテンフリー⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ケーキ→ケーキ：01356_keeki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}った→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧。
examples.english: I made a gluten-free cake using rice flour.

examples.japanese: ⟦{小麦|こむぎ}→小麦：01407_komugi⟧⟦アレルギー→アレルギー：04645_arerugii⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、グルテンフリー⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{食品|しょくひん}→食品：03247_shokuhin⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{選|えら}んでいます→選ぶ：00835_erabu⟧。
examples.english: I have a wheat allergy, so I choose gluten-free foods.

examples.japanese: ⟦{最近|さいきん}→最近：00881_saikin⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{健康|けんこう}→健康：02706_kenkou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ため→ため：01145_tame⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧グルテンフリー⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{食生活|しょくせいかつ}→食生活：21071_shokuseikatsu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}り{入|い}れる→取り入れる：04221_toriireru⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{増|ふ}えて→増える：01183_fueru⟧きて⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: Recently, more and more people are adopting a gluten-free diet for health reasons.

notes:
A direct loan from English 'gluten-free'. It is used both as a noun and as a modifier; the most natural pattern is グルテンフリー (⟦の→の：09472_no⟧) + noun.

USAGE:
Unlike English, where 'gluten-free' is purely an adjective, the Japanese form is treated grammatically as a noun. To use it before another noun, insert ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧: グルテンフリー⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{食品|しょくひん}→食品：03247_shokuhin⟧ ('gluten-free foods'). It can also stand alone as a predicate after です: '⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦パン→パン：00553_pan⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧グルテンフリーです' ('This bread is gluten-free').

The term entered Japanese mainly in the 2010s as Western-style health and fitness trends spread, and it is now common on supermarket labels, restaurant menus, and health blogs. Japan still has a much smaller market for gluten-free foods than the US or Europe, but specialty bakeries and online shops are growing.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- グルテンフリー⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{食品|しょくひん}→食品：03247_shokuhin⟧: gluten-free foods
- グルテンフリー⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{食事|しょくじ}→食事：02087_shokuji⟧: a gluten-free meal
- グルテンフリー⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{食生活|しょくせいかつ}→食生活：21071_shokuseikatsu⟧: a gluten-free diet (overall eating habits)
- グルテンフリー{食|しょく}: gluten-free food
- グルテンフリー⟦{食品|しょくひん}→食品：03247_shokuhin⟧: gluten-free foods
- グルテンフリーパン: gluten-free bread
- グルテンフリー⟦パスタ→パスタ：06768_pasuta⟧: gluten-free pasta
- グルテンフリー⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ケーキ→ケーキ：01356_keeki⟧: a gluten-free cake
- グルテンフリー⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{選|えら}ぶ→選ぶ：00835_erabu⟧: to choose gluten-free (options)
- グルテンフリー⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{試|ため}す→試す：02130_tamesu⟧: to try a gluten-free (diet)
- グルテンフリー⟦{表示|ひょうじ}→表示：03143_hyouji⟧: gluten-free labelling

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{小麦|こむぎ}→小麦：01407_komugi⟧⟦アレルギー→アレルギー：04645_arerugii⟧: wheat allergy — refers to the medical condition itself, not the diet.
- セリアック{病|びょう}: celiac disease — the autoimmune disorder that requires a strictly gluten-free diet.
- ⟦{小麦|こむぎ}→小麦：01407_komugi⟧⟦{不使用|ふしよう}→不使用：29835_fushiyou⟧: 'no wheat used' — a label found on Japanese products to indicate that wheat is not an ingredient. Not exactly the same as グルテンフリー (since barley and rye also contain gluten), but often used for the same audience.
- ⟦{米粉|こめこ}パン→米粉パン：26512_komekopan⟧: rice-flour bread — a typical Japanese gluten-free product, made from rice flour instead of wheat flour.
- ヴィーガン: vegan — a different dietary category, sometimes mentioned alongside グルテンフリー in health-food contexts.

CULTURAL NOTE:
Wheat-based foods (bread, ramen, udon, gyoza wrappers, soy sauce, tempura batter) are central to Japanese cuisine, so following a strict gluten-free diet in Japan can be challenging. Travellers with celiac disease often carry written cards explaining their condition. The Japanese soy-sauce industry has begun offering tamari (たまり) — a traditional wheat-free soy sauce — as a gluten-free option.
